summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified against the working-tree diff and the rendered CSS. Implementation is clean, additive, and correctly scoped.

comments.note: Implementation also added a 'Sortable column headers' CSS block (th.sortable, th.sort-asc::after, th.sort-desc::after) that is outside WP-001 scope. It uses only CSS variables and content values — no side-effects on color tokens — but it is undocumented scope creep.

Dark-mode component hex overrides (badge backgrounds, banners, health badges) were correctly identified as pre-existing from commit 5f1e283 and were not touched by this implementation, satisfying AC6.

summary: Reviewed the full diff of mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css. All 6 acceptance criteria are met. Token architecture is sound: --color-link correctly uses var(--color-ready) in :root (light mode unchanged) and is independently overridden to #60a5fa in [data-theme="dark"] (preserving .btn-primary white-text contrast). All 7 dark-mode token overrides are present and correctly scoped. --color-border bumped to #475569 as specified. Inline contrast-ratio comments are a positive maintainability addition. No regressions to light mode.

comments.note: The out-of-scope th.sortable / th.sort-asc::after / th.sort-desc::after block added in this commit is harmless (pure CSS, no color token side-effects) but represents undocumented scope creep. Recommend back-filling a work package or todo entry so it is tracked and doesn't accumulate silently.

--color-priority-low (#95a5a6 in :root) has no dark-mode override. This is outside WP-001 scope and not required by any AC, but #95a5a6 is a mid-grey that may read poorly on #0f172a. Consider adding --color-priority-low: #cbd5e1 (slate-300) in a follow-up.
Inline contrast-ratio annotations (e.g., '~4.7:1 with white text', '~6.0:1 on #0f172a') are a strong maintainability practice — keep this convention for any future dark-mode color additions.
